newsitem.title: UK: British utility goads U.S. firm to raise bid.
newsitem.headline: British utility goads U.S. firm to raise bid.

text.p: Britain's Northern Electric challenged bidder CE Electric Friday to raise its $1.23 billion bid for the regional electric utility as it reported results and forecasts which it claimed proved it was worth more.
"They need to get their check book out if they are going to further this bid at all," Northern Chairman David Morris told a news conference.
But CE Electric, 70 percent owned by Omaha, Neb.-based CalEnergy Co. Inc., said in a statement that Northern's results were "lackluster" and below its expectations.

The regional electricity company, said pretax profits for the six months ending Sept. 30 slipped to 50.7 million pounds ($85.1 million) from 58.7 million pounds ($97.8 million). Full year pretax profits would be more than 112 million pounds ($186 million), the company said.
"I do not think they (Northern) have announced anything that is going to make CE Electric put its price up," said one sector analyst.

Northern, which last year fended off a bid from Trafalgar House -- now part of Norway's shipbuilder and engineering group Kvaerner -- said CE Electric was going to have to pay more than the 630 pence per share ($10.50) it has offered.
Morris said CE Electric "is clearly going to have to pay a great deal more than 630 pence per share" to win control.
He said the company would be willing to talk with CE Electric "on the basis of more than 700 pence ($11.67)," but executives said at 630 pence there was nothing to discuss.
Northern has claimed that CE Electric had indicated a price of 700 pence before it launched its hostile bid in October.
CE Electric denied that claim and went on to snap up nearly 30 percent of Northern as its shares languished, weighed by concerns that the British government might block the bid.
